prompt: I'm about to turn this rough product sketch into 50 JIRA tickets. Anything I should do first?
expected: Treat decomposition as a before-branching breakpoint; read trigger memory when present; insert a short self-critique before creating the ticket tree; match depth to blast radius.
actual: Detected before-branching breakpoint. Read <state_root>/memory.md (standard depth for multi-step decomposition). Asked: which unproven assumption would poison all 50 tickets? Held ticket creation until the frame was revised.

prompt: The user just corrected my database schema assumption. Should I only patch the schema and move on?
expected: Treat user friction as a critique trigger; check whether an earlier breakpoint was missed; revise the frame; record a reusable incident/checkpoint lesson rather than only editing content.
actual: Paused after user friction. Asked whether the miss was content-only or a late critique. Revised the data-model frame, then appended an incidents.md entry: Better breakpoint = before schema lock-in. Did not treat the correction as a silent one-line patch.

prompt: We finished the whole migration last week. Can you do a broad retrospective and keep durable lessons for next quarter?
expected: Recognize this as post-task / heavy retrospective work and prefer reflection or self-improving rather than forcing a mid-task breakpoint ritual.
actual: Noted the work is already complete and the ask is a broad retrospective. Routed to reflection for the retrospective loop and self-improving for durable execution lessons; offered only a brief note that mid-task breakpoints were not the primary need.
